name: agent-plugins
description: Curated coding assistant workflows for code, notes, projects, and conversations, packaged as Claude Code plugins and Agent Skills.

plugins.name: languages
plugins.description: Per-language practice for Python and TypeScript — how the general principles are spelled in each language (types, boundaries, errors, async, tests), the traps easy to miss in it, and reproducible Jupyter notebooks. Opinionated defaults for a greenfield project; a project's own stack always outranks them.

plugins.name: code
plugins.description: Language-agnostic tools for working on a codebase that already exists — reviewing a change, diagnosing a hard bug, sweeping implementations for defects, deepening shallow interfaces, condensing documentation into short, focused docs, and re-syncing a project with the template it came from. Every routine audits before it touches anything, and each workflow skill pairs with the reference skill that defines its vocabulary.

plugins.name: obsidian-vault
plugins.description: Maintenance and authoring routines for Obsidian vaults — log formatting, inbox ingestion, knowledge harvesting, structural and accuracy audits, wikilink connectivity, file hygiene, maps of content, and deep reference notes. Every routine discovers the vault's own conventions before applying a default, and is backed by deterministic stdlib-only scripts.

plugins.name: lenses
plugins.description: Tools that change how you and your coding assistant work rather than what the code says — a high-level map of an unfamiliar area, an ultra-compressed terse mode, a one-question-at-a-time plan interview, and a stateful multi-session teaching workspace.

plugins.name: meta
plugins.description: Tools that act across all your projects rather than inside one codebase — capturing bugs, features, tasks, and ideas from any session into a central backlog repo you configure.
